paragraphs.title: The Gathering and the Building of the Altar

easy.explanation: The passage says, “when the seventh month was come.”
easy.q: In which month did the children of Israel gather themselves together?

easy.explanation: They gathered “as one man to Jerusalem.”
easy.q: How did the people gather themselves together?

answers: The altar of the God of Israel
easy.explanation: They “builded the altar of the God of Israel.”
easy.q: What did Jeshua, the priests, Zerubbabel, and their brethren build?

answers: Because fear was upon them because of the people of those countries
Because they planned to leave Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “for fear was upon them because of the people of those countries.”
medium.q: Why did they set the altar upon its bases?

medium.explanation: They offered burnt offerings “morning and evening.”
medium.q: When did they offer burnt offerings unto the LORD?

answers: Upon its foundations or established place
medium.explanation: The altar was placed upon its bases, or foundations.
medium.q: What does the phrase “upon his bases” indicate?

challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes their unity in gathering.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “as one man” suggest about the people?

answers: They built the altar and offered burnt offerings
challenge.explanation: They rebuilt the altar and began offering sacrifices before the Temple foundation was laid.
challenge.q: What did the people do before the foundation of the temple was laid?

answers: According to the customs of the surrounding peoples
According to the decision of the carpenters
As it is written in the law of Moses
challenge.explanation: The offerings were made “as it is written in the law of Moses.”
challenge.q: According to what standard did they offer the burnt offerings?

paragraphs.title: Offerings and Preparations for Building the Temple

easy.explanation: They “kept also the feast of tabernacles.”
easy.q: Which feast did the children of Israel keep?

answers: To the elders of the people
easy.explanation: They gave money “unto the masons, and to the carpenters.”
easy.q: To whom did they give money for the work?

easy.explanation: They arranged for cedar trees to be brought from Lebanon.
easy.q: What did they bring from Lebanon?

answers: The continual burnt offering, new-moon offerings, feast offerings, and freewill offerings
Only offerings made by the priests
medium.explanation: The passage lists continual, new-moon, feast, and freewill offerings.
medium.q: What offerings continued after the feast of tabernacles?

answers: To all the people of Jerusalem
To them of Zidon and to them of Tyre
medium.explanation: The goods were given to the people of Zidon and Tyre.
medium.q: To whom did they give meat, drink, and oil in exchange for cedar trees?

answers: An offering made only by officials
medium.explanation: The verse speaks of “every one that willingly offered a freewill offering.”

answers: Offerings stopped until the Temple was finished
Offerings continued while preparations for construction began
challenge.explanation: They continued offering sacrifices while preparing materials for the Temple.
challenge.q: What relationship between worship and construction is shown in these verses?

answers: Their transport was authorized by the Persian king
challenge.explanation: The cedar was obtained “according to the grant that they had of Cyrus king of Persia.”
challenge.q: What does the mention of Cyrus’s grant show about the cedar trees?

answers: The first day of the seventh month
The first day of the second month
The last day of the feast
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “From the first day of the seventh month began they to offer burnt offerings.”
challenge.q: From what day did they begin offering burnt offerings unto the LORD?

paragraphs.title: Organizing the Levites and Laying the Temple Foundations

easy.explanation: The work began “in the second year of their coming.”
easy.q: In which year did they begin organizing the work of the house of God?

answers: From twenty years old and upward
From thirteen years old and upward
From fifty years old and upward
easy.explanation: The Levites were appointed from twenty years old and upward.
easy.q: At what age were the Levites appointed to the work?

answers: The foundation of the Temple of the LORD
easy.explanation: The builders laid the foundation of the Temple.
easy.q: What was laid when the builders began their work?

answers: To set forward the work of the house of the LORD
To collect taxes from the people
To bring cedar trees from Lebanon
medium.explanation: They were appointed “to set forward the work of the house of the LORD.”
medium.q: What was the responsibility of the appointed Levites?

answers: The priests used cymbals and the Levites used trumpets
The priests used trumpets and the Levites used cymbals
medium.explanation: The priests had trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph had cymbals.
medium.q: Which instruments did the priests and Levites use?

answers: Jeshua, Kadmiel, the sons of Judah, the sons of Henadad, and their families
medium.explanation: The passage names these priests and Levites as working together.
medium.q: Who worked together to set forward the workmen?

answers: The Levites and supervisors were appointed for the work
challenge.explanation: The leaders first organized the Levites and workmen, then the foundation was laid.
challenge.q: What happened before the foundation of the Temple was laid?

answers: The praise followed David’s established ordinance
David arrived in Jerusalem that day
The music was performed outside the city
challenge.explanation: They praised the LORD “after the ordinance of David king of Israel.”
challenge.q: What does the reference to David king of Israel indicate about the music?

challenge.explanation: The priests used trumpets, the Levites used cymbals, and the people praised the LORD.
challenge.q: What accompanied the laying of the Temple foundation?

answers: Because he is good and his mercy endureth for ever
Because he gave them cedar trees
Because he ended the altar service
easy.explanation: They praised Him because “he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever.”
easy.q: Why did the people give thanks unto the LORD?

answers: Many ancient priests, Levites, and chief of the fathers
easy.explanation: The ancient men who had seen the first house wept.
easy.q: Who wept with a loud voice?
How far was the noise heard?

answers: Because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid
Because all the construction was finished
medium.explanation: The people shouted when the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.
medium.q: Why did many people shout for joy?

answers: They remembered the first house and saw the contrast with this house
medium.explanation: They had seen the first house and wept when this foundation was laid.
medium.q: Why did the ancient men weep?

answers: They made a loud cry of celebration
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a loud public expression of joy.
medium.q: What does “shouted aloud for joy” mean in this context?

answers: The people could not understand the priests
The joyful shouting could not be distinguished from the weeping
challenge.explanation: The people could not discern the noise of joy from the noise of weeping.
challenge.q: What difficulty arose in distinguishing the sounds?

answers: The same event produced different emotions in different groups
challenge.explanation: Some rejoiced at the new foundation, while the elders grieved when remembering the first house.
challenge.q: What central idea is shown by the combination of weeping and joy?

answers: The event was quiet and private
The people’s response was loud and widespread
The construction took place outside Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The combined sounds of weeping and joy were so loud that they were heard far away.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “heard afar off” emphasize?
